---
title: "Extra practice: linear regression"
---

These exercises go further than the
[Linear regression](04-linear-regression.qmd) section of the lab.
Once you've tried them,
check your answers against the
[solutions](../lecture-02-solutions/08-practice-linear-regression.qmd).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

They start from the lab's `opt_clean` data
and its model of birth weight on group, `bw_fit`.
The code below makes both again,
so this page works on its own.

```{r}
opt_clean <- opt |>
  mutate(
    Birth.outcome = str_trim(Birth.outcome),
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("C", "T"),
                   labels = c("control", "treatment"))
  ) |>
  filter(Birth.outcome == "Live birth") |>
  select(PID, Clinic, Group, Age, BMI, Birthweight, GA.at.outcome)

bw_fit <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(Birthweight ~ Group, data = opt_clean)
```

## Exercise 1: The same as a t-test?

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Run a two-sample t-test with equal variances.
Compare its t statistic and p-value
with the treatment row of `tidy(bw_fit)`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
t.test(Birthweight ~ Group, data = opt_clean, var.equal = TRUE)
```
:::

## Exercise 2: Add covariates

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Fit a model that also includes the mother's `Age`, `BMI`
   and the `Clinic` she enrolled at.
2. Use `glance()` to find how many rows the model used (`nobs`).
   Why is it fewer than the rows in `opt_clean`?
3. Did the treatment estimate change much?
   Why might that be in a randomized trial?

```{r}
#| eval: false
bw_fit_adj <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(Birthweight ~ ____, data = opt_clean)

tidy(bw_fit_adj, conf.int = TRUE)
glance(bw_fit_adj)
```
:::

## Exercise 3: Check the fit

Residuals, the observed minus the fitted values,
should scatter evenly around 0.

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Plot the residuals of `bw_fit` against its fitted values.
What do you see?

```{r}
#| eval: false
augment(bw_fit, new_data = opt_clean) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .pred, y = ____)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 5, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)
```
:::

## Exercise 4: Gestational age

The trial's main outcome was gestational age at birth
(`GA.at.outcome`, in days).

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

Fit a linear regression of gestational age on `Group`,
then adjust for `Age`, `BMI` and `Clinic`.
Did the treatment change gestational age?
:::
